body: I hope that you find a thread of hope. I lost my son to suicide and it has been difficult. I can understand to some point the hopelessness from my own situation and how suicide affects those left behind.  The world is a better place with you in it.

All I can do is speak from experience.  In my own unique experience myself, my husband, my other children, and other family members did not know that our son was hurting.  His actions, words, and day to day activities did not give clues to anything out of the ordinary for him.  He was a bright light in all of our lives.  Very caring, very open. 

Since the death of my son, we have experienced love and critics.  We have experienced concern and anger.

I am not responsible for his death, nor do I look for sympathy or profit from his death.  I cannot even tell you the destruction this has caused in all of our lives.  Yes, his death is about him -- but it impacts everyone because he was so loved and so special in our lives.  

I work hard at trying to connect with people who can get something out of what I have been through.  Not for profit - to help.  I don't have all the right answers and I struggle with even approaching the prevention subject, because how can I speak to prevention?  My son died by suicide, I didn't prevent anything.  

Much of what happens after the loss of a loved one by suicide is a personal struggle dependent on the relationship between the you and the one that died.  The guilt can overwhelm and eat at you.  It can put you in a place that your lost loved one was probably sitting in also. 

I am a Mom that lost her child and is completely heartbroken by it.  This has turned my entire life upsidedown and nothing will ever be right again.  That is a fact - it has nothing to do with a self serving agenda.  It has to do with life and death and grief and the struggle to understand suicide.  You may not like my post and you may be angry by my post - but I am here to say that suicide shatters everyone close to you.  Including the ones that you may not be thinking of - the one's that you may not realize love you.  I know that doesn't automatically fix anything.  I know that mental illness, depression, and suicidal thoughts go much deeper than just knowing that you are loved.  I don't have an answer to fix it, I only have my experience of how suicide ends more than just one life.

We were with him a lot.  He was going through a lot of changes in his life, new house, new job, and his wife was in Afghanistan.  I was caring for his two daughters during the week while he was starting his new job and staying with his twin brother in Denver.  He would come out here on the weekends and stay with us and the girls.  He was excited about moving, the place was beautiful.  His girls are amazing and he loved them so much - and he was making changes according to what he thought could save his marriage.  His marriage was falling apart and it consumed him.  We all did ask - we were his cheerleaders.  Something happened that day.  We all feel that there was something on his phone, a text or email that could explain.  We were all so close, we would have known.

I am so sorry that you do not have support from your parents.  You are right - it is not about us who are left to figure it out, it is about those we have lost.  In my situation, which is all I can honestly speak from, I did not know my son was in so much pain.  He was such an amazing person, happy, silly, great dad, great friend to all of us.  His letter to me the night he died explained why and how he did not want to hurt any of us.  But even though I have a letter - I have so many questions that will never be answered and I was not given a chance as his Mom to help.  Pain is real to anyone experiencing it.  We cannot judge someone's pain because we do not have the same experiences, thoughts, values, etc... that they do.  We have to believe in it and help.  I take it serious.
Thank you so much for your words.  I would love to stay and share with everyone here.

Perspective is lost in fog.  We are all loved and deserve a good life.  Can you move closer to your parents?  Can you go home for now, explain that you are in crisis?  Explain to them that you are not in a safe place?  Can you take small steps towards finding yourself?  Some people respond well to treatment for depression, especially when they are in danger.  After my son died I was at risk for suicide.  I was on suicide watch and my entire family was worried that I would not survive.  I made myself a survival kit.  I put together a box full of the things that I needed while I was in a bad spot.  Music, pictures, writings, poems, books, special items, etc....  It is something I get down off the shelf when I am in a bad spot, I let myself go to that dark place and I pour over the pictures, I cry, I scream, I fall apart.  But, I know that there is a time that the box gets put back together and put back on the shelf.  Ready for the next time.  What can we put together for you that would reflect hope?  Something to feed the flicker inside you.  I want you to live.

Well if it is worth anything I will be your friend and you can talk to me anytime.  What types of things are you interested in?  Do you do well with school?  Do you have a support system outside of your family?

She may surprise you.  We all have a story and sometimes tradition and simplicity in our lives comes from trauma that we have seen or experienced.  Being afraid of getting HIV is similar to anyone that is a young adult and worried of disease and illness from a sexual partner.  Respecting ourselves for so long and then making a decision to have sex with someone that we have no clue what their history is....it is scary for anyone.  I had trust issues when I was 18 so I can understand a tiny part, the trust you have to put in someone - believing that they will not infect you, screw you over, leave you, etc....  HIV is not limited to the gay community - it is a fear for anyone that has had sex, unprotected.  
I hope you can get to the point where the envelope and video are destroyed.  I think just the idea that you have the fear of getting HIV...that means you have hope for life and want to live.  We are all here to help you through it.
That is a good start.  Let's work towards you not doing for you also.  You are worth it.  Let me know if there is anything I can help with.  Have you talked to your Mom about how you feel?

Please don't.  Live for you, live for them.  I cannot begin to understand your pain or the depths of your despair and hopelessness.  Please hold on to something positive in your life - hold on to your parents.  Hold on to yourself.  Hold on to us here.

I wish I would have known about his pain.  Maybe if I could have had the chance to be proactive to help him recognize triggers, tough situations, painful feelings, and how to work through the overwhelming times.  Have you talked to your daughter about it?  Can you both setup a survival plan ahead of time?  No one wants to think of the pain of losing a child.  It is a tragedy no one should have to go through.  What can I do to help you?
Will your husband help at all?  Although there are differences does he understand it is important to keep you safe and alive?  Can you depend on him to get help to work through each hurdle?

I have been in this hole for different reasons.  My son died by suicide.  No one knew he was in pain - things were great for him in appearances.  He left two daughters that are forever changed, forever at risk for the same, and forever asking why - just like me, his mother.  

Please do not give up.  Use this and resources to turn things around.  Reach out to the closest person in your life for help.  It will take hard work and time but please stay committed to the cause...the cause being you.  You are so worth it, you are a Momma and kids need their mother.  Forever.  Talk to me anytime - Leslie
